root_idea.summary: The root is oriented primarily toward whiteness, from which salt is understood to have received its name, with related extensions involving salinity, coloring, pleasantness, and salt-based practices.
root_idea.development: The lexical development proceeds from whiteness to the pale substance salt and saline water, and then to actions involving salt, salt-derived descriptions of color and beauty, and figurative bonds associated with sharing salt.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under the normalized citation form مِلْحٌ.

senses.definition: Saline or briny water; water whose taste has become characteristically salty.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, مِلْحٌ occurs in the construction مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ, describing water that is salt and intensely briny. This Quranic sense concerns saline water rather than every broader classical use of the headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Salt, the substance used to season or make food pleasant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary concrete noun; it may be feminine or, less commonly, masculine, and has the plural مِلَاحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To salt food, fish, meat, or a hide; to put an appropriate amount of salt into a cooking pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used for salting provisions or hides and for seasoning a pot in the proper quantity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put an excessive amount of salt into something and thereby spoil it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the excessive or destructive counterpart to ordinary salting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Salted fish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive participial form is preferred in this usage over مَالِحٌ according to the cited lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed camels, sheep, or goats with salty earth or earth mixed with a greater quantity of salt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This practice is described for animals unable to obtain the relevant salt-tolerant plants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rub an animal’s palate with salt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is typically a camel, sheep, or goat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suckle or give suck; suckling, a single feed at the breast, or a sucker.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The branch includes the act of nursing, a single suck or feeding, and the child or creature that suckles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk, especially milk received through nursing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a lexical extension associated with suckling and is distinct from the concrete salt and saline-water senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become someone’s foster-brother through shared nursing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived verb refers to the relationship created by suckling from the same woman, not to literally sucking one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This figurative Form III usage is associated with sharing salt or food with another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fat; fat or fatness, especially the fatness of a camel or other animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources include a camel destined for slaughter that is fat or somewhat fat, and مِلْحٌ used figuratively for fat or a small degree of fatness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To possess milk; by extension, to have fat livestock or other beasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV construction is predicated of a people or group possessing such resources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For camels to come to salt water to drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an intransitive Form IV construction describing the camels’ arrival at saline water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be goodly, beautiful, pretty, pleasing, or attractive; a person whose counsel is valued or whose company is pleasant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The branch applies to appearance, color, hearing, conduct, counsel, and agreeable companionship; it is not restricted to any particular gender or object class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce or affect goodly, graceful, beautiful, or facetious speech; a witty or attractive story, saying, or bon mot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage concerns speech, stories, and conversational style, including affecting cleverness or grace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find or esteem someone or something beautiful or pleasing; to grace or recommend someone by speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The first construction expresses evaluation, while the second is an imperative request for favorable recommendation or embellishment through speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coloration marked by whiteness mixed with black, gray, blue, or another hue; variegated white-and-dark coloring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description applies to hair, wool, animals, eyes, clothing, trees, dew, and other things. It can describe a white color predominating over black, dusty or clear whiteness, or gray-blue tending toward white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main body, fathomless deep, or vast expanse of the sea whose extremities cannot be seen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized noun for a great open stretch of sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Knowledge, science, or learning; by extension, learned people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources record both the abstract sense of knowledge and the collective reference to men of learning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sacred or inviolable bond, compact, obligation, or confederacy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative sense is associated with sharing salt or food and the obligation thereby created to honor the relationship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the idiom “his salt is upon his knees,” to lack good faith in keeping promises or obligations; by extension, to be easily angered, ill-disposed, or contentious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom has several closely related explanations: obligations are quickly forgotten or violated, anger is easily stirred, or the person is habitually engaged in altercation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A salt-tasting plant of the ḥamḍ class.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant is described as useful to camels and sheep and as growing in salty or depressed tracts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for certain plants or plant products, including a white elongated grape, a small sweet dried fig, and a species of arāk tree with variegated coloring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derivation is variously associated with the color ملحة or with a hot or salt-like taste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller, possessor, or trader in salt; one who provides salt as travelling provision.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This occupational noun is distinct from the homonymous maritime occupation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sailor, shipman, seaman, or mariner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The occupation is named in relation to constant work upon salt water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who continually attends a river or waterway to keep its mouth in proper condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized occupational use distinct from both salt selling and sailing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where salt is generated or produced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived place noun includes the synonymous form مَمْلَحَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A container or receptacle in which salt is kept.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may refer to a vessel or any comparable object used for holding salt.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease or swelling in the hock, hock-tendon, or corresponding part of a horse’s leg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition is described as less severe than جَرَذٌ; أَمْلَحُ can describe a horse affected by it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for a winter month or winter days associated with whiteness from snow or hoarfrost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is variously applied in the reported calendars to Jumādā al-Ākhirah, Jumādā al-Ūlā, or one of the months called Kānūn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of a camel’s back extending from the withers toward the rump, including the region beneath the hump and its vertebrae.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term has several closely related anatomical specifications, including the flesh or middle of the back and the portion beneath the hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A curiosity or extraordinary thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized nominal use distinct from the color and witty-speech senses of مُلْحَةٌ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The salt-water construction is covered by the Quran-attested saline-water sense.
Salt waters and salt wells belong to the saline-water branch.
The target definition explicitly includes learned people.
Proper-name or external bird reference, not an independent lexical branch here.
Proper-name identification of a troop, not an independent lexical meaning.

cautions: The two Quranic occurrences attest the saline-water use of مِلْحٌ; the contextual gloss “salty” does not by itself establish the broader classical branches.
